summary: The change stays within the permitted files, and the live-PID checks and Python 3.10 syntax look sound. The prune tests and full suite could not be verified: this read-only sandbox has no usable temporary directory; the full suite discovered 89 tests. Static review found two deletion safety races and one status check gap.

findings.evidence: `_real_job_dir(root, name)` uses `lstat`, but lines 546 and 554 then call path-based `read_job(name)` and `refresh_job(job)`. `refresh_job` opens `JOB_ROOT/name/job.lock` and can write job metadata.
findings.problem: If the entry becomes a symlink after `lstat`, selection can follow it and create or modify files outside JOB_ROOT, even during a dry run. The new no-follow lock protects only the later deletion phase.
findings.suggestion: Use directory-relative, no-follow opens throughout selection and refresh; do not call the path-based refresh on an entry that can change into a symlink.

findings.evidence: After verifying `hidden` at lines 519–521, `_prune_one` exits `_locked_job_dir` and calls `shutil.rmtree(root / hidden)` at line 531.
findings.problem: The verified directory, or the path to JOB_ROOT, can be replaced before `rmtree` resolves it. A different directory, including an unfinished job or a directory outside the job root, can then be removed. Rename-then-verify does not close this final path race.
findings.suggestion: Keep deletion anchored to the verified directory and job-root descriptors, with no path lookup that can switch to another directory after verification.

findings.evidence: `_prune_reason` excludes only `starting`, `running`, `canceling`, and live PIDs; any other status with an old `finished_at` returns `None`.
findings.problem: An unrecognized or future unfinished status is treated as finished and can be deleted, contrary to the finished-jobs-only requirement.
findings.suggestion: Accept only known terminal statuses as prune candidates; skip every other status.
